title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
description: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment or fine.
elements: Driving or riding a vehicle
Operation occurred on a public way
Manner of driving was rash or negligent
Act endangered human life or was likely to cause hurt/injury
exceptions: Acts committed on strictly private land not open to public traffic
Involuntary mechanical failure without prior negligence of the driver
penalty: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 6 months, or with fine which may extend to 1,000 rupees, or with both.
source_name: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Govt of India

title: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others
description: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine.
elements: Grievous hurt was suffered by a person (e.g. fracture, severe organ injury)
Hurt was caused by the accused's act
Act was done rashly or negligently
Act endangered human life or personal safety
exceptions: Consent given in good faith for medical intervention
Accident without criminal intention or knowledge
penalty: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to 10,000 rupees, or both.
source_name: Ministry of Law and Justice, India

title: Causing death by negligence
description: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
elements: Death of a human being occurred
Death was directly caused by the act of the accused
Act was rash or negligent
Act does not amount to culpable homicide (lack of intention to kill)
exceptions: Supervening medical negligence by third parties breaking causation
Pure unpreventable mechanical act of god
penalty: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
source_name: Ministry of Law and Justice, India

title: Duty of driver in case of accident and injury to a person
description: When any person is injured or any property of a third party is damaged as a result of an accident in which a motor vehicle is involved, the driver of the vehicle or other person in charge of the vehicle shall take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person and report to the nearest police station.
elements: Motor vehicle involved in accident
Injury caused to person or property damage caused
Driver failed to secure immediate medical attention or convey injured to hospital
Driver failed to inform nearest police officer/station within 24 hours
exceptions: Driver prevented by mob violence or imminent threat of physical assault from remaining at scene (must report to police immediately upon reaching safety)
penalty: Fine up to 5,000 rupees or imprisonment up to 3 months for first offence.
source_name: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, India

title: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs
description: Whoever, while driving, or attempting to drive, a motor vehicle has in his blood, a quantity of alcohol exceeding 30 mg. per 100 ml. of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser or blood test, shall be punishable.
elements: Driving or attempting to drive motor vehicle
Blood alcohol content (BAC) exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml blood
Detection verified by breath analyzer, blood lab analysis, or clinical medical test
exceptions: Administered under valid medical prescription without warning against driving
penalty: First offence: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to 10,000 rupees. Subsequent offence: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to 15,000 rupees.
source_name: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, India

statute: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Indian Evidence Act Sec 45 Equivalent)
title: Opinions of experts
description: When the Court has to form an opinion upon a point of foreign law or of science or art, or as to identity of handwriting or finger impressions, the opinions upon that point of persons specially skilled in such science, art or law are relevant facts.
elements: Court requires technical/scientific evaluation
Witness possesses special skill, qualification, or medical degree
Opinion directly concerns medical report, post-mortem, chemical analysis, or forensic finding
exceptions: Opinion is purely speculative or unsupported by physical evidence/reasoning
source_name: Ministry of Law and Justice, India
